bankFile.title: Direct deposit
bankFile.hint: The file instructs the bank to credit each EFT employee. Once generated it is frozen, hashed and numbered; every download is recorded.
bankFile.regenerateLabel: Why is a replacement needed? The existing file stays on record and is marked superseded. If it has already gone to the bank, do not send both.
bankFile.regeneratePlaceholder: e.g. bank rejected the first transmission
bankFile.multipleLive: This pay run has more than one file that has not been superseded. Send exactly ONE to the bank — releasing both pays every employee twice.
bankFile.noProfile: No originating bank profile is set up for payroll. Add one in Setup → Payment operations: the originator id, routing and company identification are assigned by your bank and are never defaulted.
bankFile.excludedTitle: Not on the file — reconcile these against the payday
bankFile.auditTitle: Activity — who generated and who downloaded

exclusion.default: No bank details on file — paid by cheque
exclusion.eftFallback: Set to EFT but has no approved bank details — paid by cheque

runTypeHint.regular: The schedule's normal payroll: salary, approved time, recurring components and deductions.
runTypeHint.bonus: Off-cycle pay for bonuses and commissions. No salary, time or recurring deductions; earnings are taxed on the bonus method.
runTypeHint.termination: Final pay for departing employees. Includes the accrued vacation balance as a payout.

newRun.employeesHint: A final pay run pays out and clears every accrued bank, so it runs only for the employees named here.
newRun.noTerminated: No employee on this schedule has a termination date on file. Record it on the employee first — a final cheque cannot be calculated without one.
newRun.description: Confirm the period this run covers. The schedule’s next period is prefilled; change the dates for an off-cycle or catch-up run.
newRun.payDateHint: The date employees are paid. Statutory rates are resolved from this date.
newRun.invalidWindow: Period end must fall on or after the start, and the pay date on or after the period end.
newRun.notBegun: This period starts {date} and has not begun. Choose a period that is under way or complete.

profiles.noSchedules: Create a pay schedule before setting up payroll profiles.

labourJurisdiction.help: The labour jurisdiction whose employment standards govern this employment — its statutory holiday calendar and its holiday-pay formula. Leave it on "from the province of employment", which is right for almost every employment; set it only when a different labour jurisdiction regulates the employer of record, such as a federally regulated employer. It does not change withholding, which always follows the province of employment.

paymentMethod.help: How this employee is paid. Leave it on the party default unless this person is paid differently from the rest — a cheque for someone with no bank details on file, for instance. The pay run splits the payday between the two rails and funds each separately.

cta.title: Set up payroll
cta.description: A guided first run: country packs, control accounts, a pay schedule, remittance vendors, and pay rails — the same checks a pay run verifies before it calculates.
cta.missing: {count, plural, one {# required item} other {# required items}} still to configure.

packs.title: Install your country packs
packs.description: A pack is the statutory engine for one jurisdiction: its withholding math, pay components, holidays, and filings.
packs.note: Installing a pack seeds its statutory pay components and switches on that jurisdiction's withholding engine. Existing components are never overwritten, and a pack can be added later by re-running this wizard.

accounts.title: Control accounts
accounts.description: Where wages and net pay post, and the liability account behind each statutory withholding the installed packs declare.
accounts.wageExpenseHelp: The expense account gross wages are debited to when a pay run commits.
accounts.netPayHelp: The liability account net pay is credited to until the payday funds leave the bank.
accounts.slotHelp: The liability account this statutory withholding accrues in until it is remitted.

schedule.title: Pay schedule
schedule.description: The pay calendar: how often people are paid and which period ends anchor the cycle.
schedule.name: Name
schedule.nameHelp: How this calendar appears on runs and employee profiles — e.g. “Biweekly — all staff”.
schedule.frequencyHelp: How often this calendar pays. Periods per year follows the statutory table for the frequency.
schedule.periodsHelp: The statutory period count the withholding engine annualizes with — 52 weekly, 26 biweekly, 24 semi-monthly, 12 monthly.
schedule.anchorHelp: Any real period-end date on this calendar; every other period is projected forward and backward from it.
schedule.noPermission: Creating pay schedules needs the Setup permission. Ask an administrator to add one on the Pay schedules tab, then continue.

vendors.title: Remittance vendors
vendors.description: The vendor each statutory authority is remitted to, as declared by the installed packs.
vendors.help: Withheld amounts accrue against this vendor so a remittance raises a normal payable to the authority.
vendors.note: Vendors are ordinary vendor records — create the authority under Entities → Vendors first if it does not exist yet, then pick it here.

rails.title: Pay rails
rails.description: How net pay leaves the bank on payday: direct deposit files, and what happens when an employee meant for EFT has no bank details.
rails.eftNone: No payroll-capable originator profile exists yet. Direct-deposit files need one; until then employees are paid by cheque.
rails.manageProfiles: Manage originator profiles in Payment operations

review.title: Review & finish
review.description: What this org's payroll now looks like, and what a pay run would still stop on.
review.allClear: All required configuration is in place. A pay run can calculate.
review.seedNote: Finishing re-runs the statutory component seed for each installed pack — idempotent, and existing components are never overwritten.

done.title: Payroll is ready
done.description: Add employees and their payroll profiles, then start the first run.

settingsPage.title: Payroll
settingsPage.description: Install payroll country packs, wire the posting accounts, and manage pay schedules, components, and union agreements.

accounts.title: Control accounts
accounts.description: Where wages, employer burden, and net pay post. Statutory withholding accounts are configured per installed country pack below.

posting.title: Posting
posting.description: How time-driven wages hit the ledger, and who statutory withholdings are remitted to.

wagesTo.help: Labor clearing washes the standard cost posted at time approval; it needs the labor clearing control account from Labor Costing.

fields.rqRemittancePartyIdHelp: Vendor billed for Québec source deductions remitted on form TPZ-1015.R — a QC employee's QPP, QPP2 and QPIP route here, never to the CRA vendor.

payday.eftDescription: Direct deposit files are drawn from a payroll-capable originator profile. Profiles are managed in Payment operations; this panel reports their state.
payday.eftNone: No payroll-capable originator profile exists yet. Until one is configured, direct-deposit employees rely on the cheque fallback.
payday.eftManage: Manage originator profiles in Payment operations

packs.componentCount: {count, plural, one {# statutory component installed} other {# statutory components installed}}
packs.hint: Installing a pack seeds the statutory pay components and switches on that jurisdiction's withholding engine. Existing components are never overwritten.

canada.title: Canada
canada.description: Statutory withholding for Canadian pay runs, remittances, and year-end.
canada.edition: {edition, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}} edition (effective {effective})
canada.coverage: All provinces & territories. Quebec: QPP, QPIP, and the federal side; provincial income tax is administered by Revenu Québec and is not included.
canada.components: Statutory pay components: base pay, overtime, bonus, vacation, income tax, CPP, EI, QPIP.

us.title: United States
us.description: Federal statutory withholding for US pay runs: income tax, Social Security, Medicare, and unemployment.
us.engine: IRS Pub 15-T percentage-method engine (2026) with W-4 Steps 2–4 and pre-2020 allowances.
us.coverage: Federal plus the nine no-withholding states (AK, FL, NV, NH, SD, TN, TX, WA, WY). State income tax withholding ships in a later wave.
us.components: Statutory pay components: federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare (incl. Additional Medicare), FUTA, and SUI.
us.config: SUI rates and wage bases are experience-rated per employer. Enter yours under Accounts & posting.

packs.uninstallConfirm: Remove this pack’s statutory components and switch off its withholding engine? Uninstalling is blocked while employees or payroll records still depend on the pack.

packAccounts.none: No payroll country pack is installed yet, so there are no statutory withholding accounts to configure.

CA.title: Canada — CRA statutory accounts
CA.description: Liability accounts for the amounts the CRA pack withholds and accrues. Each choice applies to every component the slot covers (employee and employer sides together).

US.title: United States — federal statutory accounts
US.description: Liability accounts for the amounts the US pack withholds and accrues. Each choice applies to every component the slot covers (employee and employer sides together).

packAccounts.ratesLink: Rates you supply — unemployment, health levies — are on the Statutory Rates tab.

usConfig.title: Unemployment rates
usConfig.description: FUTA and state unemployment are employer-paid. SUI rates are experience-rated per employer, so they are entered here, never assumed.
usConfig.futaRateHelp: As a decimal: 0.006 is the standard 0.6% after the full state credit. Raise it for credit-reduction states.
usConfig.suiHelp: One row per state you employ in: your assessed rate as a decimal (0.027 = 2.7%) and the state’s taxable wage base.

caConfig.title: Employer payroll taxes
caConfig.description: Employer-paid taxes the CA pack accrues each run: workers' compensation premiums and the Ontario Employer Health Tax.
caConfig.ehtRateHelp: As a percent: 1.95 is the top Ontario rate. Your rate depends on total Ontario payroll.
caConfig.ehtExemptionHelp: Ontario remuneration exempt each year ($1,000,000 for most eligible private employers; associated employers share one exemption).
caConfig.wcbNote: Workers' compensation (WCB/WSIB) rates and the annual assessable maximum are set per rate class on worker-comp groups, under People setup.

stubPassword.title: Emailed pay-stub password
stubPassword.description: Encrypt emailed pay stubs and derive each employee's password from a rule you publish to your staff.
stubPassword.unavailable: PDF encryption is unavailable on this server — the qpdf tool is not installed.
stubPassword.expressionHelp: Tokens: {surname}, {givenName}, {employeeNumber} (add :3 for the first three characters) and {dob} with a format (MMDDYYYY, DDMMYYYY, YYYYMMDD, MMDDYY, DDMMYY, YYMMDD, MMDD, YYYY). Add |upper or |lower to change case. Example: {surname:3|upper}{dob:MMDDYYYY}.

derivedPreview.title: Preview a derived earnings rule
derivedPreview.description: See which employees and days a rule would hit, and what it would pay, before you enable it.
derivedPreview.noRules: No derived earnings rules are configured yet.
derivedPreview.pickRule: Choose a rule to preview the period.
derivedPreview.empty: This rule pays nothing over the selected period.
derivedPreview.grossEstimated: This rule pays a percentage of gross. The preview estimates gross from approved time and the effective wage; the pay run's own calculation is authoritative.
derivedPreview.excludedDescription: These employees are kept out by the rule's exclusion list — the deletion nobody has to remember any more.
derivedPreview.coverageTitle: This rule cannot settle the month yet
derivedPreview.coverageBody: Some equipment charges in the settled month do not record which operator ran the unit, so the incentive cannot tell who is owed. It refuses rather than pay on the charges that happen to be attributed, which would under-pay. Record the operator on those charges, or narrow this rule so they fall outside it.

paymentMethods.title: How wages are paid
paymentMethods.description: An employee with no approved bank details is paid by cheque. This decides what happens when someone set to direct deposit has none.
paymentMethods.fallback: Pay by cheque when direct-deposit details are missing
paymentMethods.fallbackOn: The run continues and the employee is included in the cheque batch, with a warning on the readiness step.
paymentMethods.fallbackOff: The run is blocked until the employee has approved bank details or is switched to cheque.

holidayCalendar.title: Statutory holiday calendar
holidayCalendar.description: The days this jurisdiction observes, with your own elections applied. Statutory days come from the country pack and cannot be switched off; optional and company days are configured on the Holidays tab.
holidayCalendar.empty: No holidays are observed in this year.
holidayCalendar.noMandate: This jurisdiction mandates no statutory holiday pay, so the calendar drives closures and working-day arithmetic only. Days off may still be paid under your own policy.
holidayCalendar.payRule: How a day's holiday pay is computed
holidayCalendar.normalDay: the wages of one normal working day, from the employee’s recorded work schedule
holidayCalendar.normalDayStandardHours: for employees working at least the jurisdiction's standard hours,
holidayCalendar.beforeTheWeek: before the week of the holiday
holidayCalendar.daysWorkedOrEarned: days worked or on which wages were earned
holidayCalendar.daysEntitledToPay: days the employee was paid, or entitled to be paid, for

statHolidayPay.title: Statutory holiday pay
statHolidayPay.description: Calculate statutory holiday pay and worked-holiday premiums on each pay run, using the formula the employee's jurisdiction declares. Employees in a jurisdiction with no declared formula are refused by name when a holiday falls in the period.

rates.title: Statutory rates
rates.description: Rates no publication can supply, or that agencies publish per region or per registered account. Everything else — tax brackets, contribution maximums, credit amounts — comes from the country pack and cannot be edited here.
rates.noPacks: No installed country pack declares an employer-entered statutory rate. Install a pack on the Country packs tab.
rates.yearHelp: Statutory rates are assigned for a tax year — a state rate notice, a credit-reduction determination, a provincial exemption. Rates entered for one year never reinterpret another year's payroll.
rates.empty: No statutory rates are entered for this year.
rates.regionHelp: The region the rate applies in. A rate entered for one region is never applied to another.
rates.accountHelp: This rate is assigned to a registered account, so an employer with two accounts in one region has two rates. Leave as All accounts to use one value for every account in the region.
rates.subRegionHelp: The taxing jurisdiction inside the region — a Pennsylvania PSD code, an Ohio municipality, a Michigan city. Each one sets its own rate, so each one is entered separately; a jurisdiction with no rate on file refuses the pay run by name rather than withholding nothing.

workSchedules.title: Work schedules
workSchedules.description: The hours and days each employee is normally scheduled to work. Several jurisdictions compute statutory holiday pay from this — a normal working day's wages — and will refuse to calculate rather than assume an eight-hour day for someone whose schedule is not recorded.
workSchedules.drawerDescription: Applies from the start date until it is superseded or ended. Holiday pay for a past period always resolves against the pattern in force then, never today's.

pattern.cycleHint: A cycle of days that repeats — seven days for an ordinary week, fourteen for a compressed fortnight, eight for a four-on four-off rotation.
pattern.variesHint: No regular schedule; hours are set period by period. This is a real answer, not a blank one — several jurisdictions pay a varying-hours employee by a different formula, and recording it is what lets them calculate.

summary.total: {hours} hours over {days} working days per cycle.

help.scope: The most specific schedule wins: one employee beats a job title, which beats a trade, then a department, then a subsidiary, then everyone. The same order wages and entitlement limits resolve in.
help.effectiveFrom: Compared against the WORK DATE, never today. Someone who moves from full time to part time in March still has January's holiday pay computed on the full-time pattern.
help.pattern: Whether the employee works a repeating pattern, or has no regular schedule at all. The difference decides which formula several jurisdictions use.
help.cycleDays: How many days before the pattern repeats. Seven is the ordinary week. Fourteen expresses a nine-day fortnight; eight expresses a four-on four-off rotation that deliberately never lines up with the week.
help.cycleAnchor: The day the cycle starts counting from. For a weekly pattern this is a Sunday, so the boxes below are labelled Sunday to Saturday.
help.hours: The hours normally worked at each position of the cycle. Leave a day blank for a day off. These hours are what a normal working day's holiday pay is calculated from, so a four-day ten-hour week is worth ten hours a holiday, not eight.

remittances.title: Payroll remittances
remittances.description: Accrued withholdings and employer contributions by destination for a period. Creating a bill debits the liability accounts and hands payment to AP.
remittances.empty: No committed pay runs with remittable amounts in this period.
remittances.assignVendor: Assign a vendor on the components
remittances.context: Gross payroll {gross} · {employees, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}} in the period
remittances.billCreated: Draft bill {number} created. Review and post it in AP.
remittances.apNote: Remittance bills are ordinary vendor bills:

yearEnd.title: Year-end
yearEnd.description: Every annual and quarterly return the installed payroll packs declare, built from committed pay stubs — every box reconciles to the stub traces.
yearEnd.noFilings: No payroll year-end filings are declared for this organization.

cadence.annualHelp: Filed once per tax year (T4, W-2, RL-1). The tax-year picker above selects which year's population is shown.
cadence.quarterlyHelp: Filed once per calendar quarter (Form 941) — the population table shows one row per quarter within the selected tax year.

filings.rowCount: {count, plural, =0 {No rows} one {# row} other {# rows}}

issue.reasonHelp: Block 16 is the employer's declaration of why earnings stopped. Choosing a reason includes this employee in the ROE Web file; leaving it unset keeps them out.
issue.commentRequired: A comment is required for this reason code.

lifecycle.title: Filing status
lifecycle.help: An issued filing is evidence of what was declared to the agency, so it is never overwritten: a correction is a new artifact that supersedes it, and the original file stays downloadable. Amounts are always recomputed from committed pay stubs — correct the payroll data, then amend.
lifecycle.resurrectedCount: Cancelled but still in the ledger
lifecycle.noArtifact: No electronic file — the slip snapshot below is the record.
lifecycle.correctionHelp: Amending restates a slip that should exist; cancelling declares that the slip should never have existed. The figures are recomputed from committed pay stubs — they are never typed over — so correct the payroll data first and the amendment follows.
lifecycle.unfiledHelp: This slip has not been recorded as filed, so there is nothing to correct.
lifecycle.addedHelp: This slip appeared after the return was filed. A slip discovered later is filed as an additional original, not as a correction, and that is not produced here — file it through the agency's own service.
lifecycle.absentHelp: The payroll ledger no longer produces this slip, so there is nothing to restate. Cancel it so the agency stops holding it.
lifecycle.resurrectedHelp: This slip was cancelled, but the payroll ledger still produces it. Void or adjust the underlying run, or the next return will file it again.

status.resurrected: Cancelled but still in the ledger

run.title: {label}
run.help: Everyone this filing covers, with the figures it will carry. Produce the file only once the rows are right — an issued filing is evidence, and correcting it means an amendment rather than an edit.

separations.title: Separations
separations.description: Separation filings the installed payroll packs declare — due within days of an interruption of earnings, per employee event, not at year-end.
separations.noFilings: No payroll separation filings are declared for this organization.

run.title: Issue {label}
run.help: A separation filing is due within days of the interruption of earnings — issue it from this run, per employee, rather than waiting for year-end.

register.title: Payroll register
register.totals: Totals ({count, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}})

entitlements.title: Pay banks
entitlements.hint: Banked time, vacation, and any balance this employee owes back. Balances are the entitlement ledger — they move through payroll, never by editing a number.
entitlements.noPlans: No entitlement plans are configured for this organization yet.
entitlements.hoursAtWage: {hours} hours at the current wage of {wage}/h
entitlements.owedBack: Owed back to the employer — recouped from future pay.

paymentMethod.help: Leave as the default to follow the employee record: direct deposit when approved bank details exist, otherwise a printed cheque.

openingBalances.title: Opening balances
openingBalances.description: Everything each employee carries in from your previous payroll system: statutory year-to-date, the annual caps they have partly used, and their vacation and banked-time balances. Nothing else supplies these, so every ceiling and every bank restarts at zero without them.
openingBalances.hint: Copy these from the outgoing provider's year-to-date report as at the day before your first pay period here. Leave an employee blank if they had no pay from you earlier in the year.
openingBalances.rejected: Nothing was saved — fix these first.
openingBalances.empty: No employees have an active payroll profile yet.
openingBalances.componentHelp: How much of this component's annual cap the employee has already used this year, at your previous payroll system. Without it the cap restarts at zero and the employee can contribute a second full annual limit.
openingBalances.componentInertHelp: This component no longer has an annual cap, so the amount below changes nothing and cannot be edited. It is kept because somebody entered it and a cap may be set again.

entitlements.title: Bank carry-ins (vacation, banked time)
entitlements.asOfHelp: The adoption date the carry-in is dated. A pay run only counts movements dated on or before its pay date, so this must fall before your first pay run here. It is not a tax year: a bank has one lifetime balance.
entitlements.rejected: Nothing was saved — fix these first.
entitlements.empty: No employees have an active payroll profile yet.
entitlements.noPlans: No entitlement plans are set up, so there is no bank to carry a balance into.
entitlements.legacyBody: These employees carry a vacation balance on the retired opening-balances column that no bank shows. It is a liability nobody is tracking. Load it here, or run scripts/migrate-vacation-to-entitlements.ts to replay the whole history.
entitlements.legacyPrefill: Copy them into the Vacation column
entitlements.moneyHelp: The balance carried in, in dollars. Banks are stored as the money they were earned at, and displayed as hours at the employee's current wage.
entitlements.hoursHelp: The balance carried in, in hours.
entitlements.oweHelp: A balance the EMPLOYEE owes the employer, so it is negative — enter −1200 for an outstanding 1,200. It is recouped from future pay until it reaches exactly zero.

readiness.jurisdictionEmployee: Employee jurisdiction disagrees with the paying entity

parallelRun.title: Parallel run
parallelRun.description: Check a pay period against the payroll system you are leaving, penny by penny. Import the old provider's register, pick the run that covers the same period, and compare.
parallelRun.compareFailed: The comparison could not be run.
parallelRun.tolerancesDescription: Every component compares exactly by default. Add an allowance only where the old system genuinely rounds differently — it will be shown on every comparison that uses it.
parallelRun.noTolerances: No tolerance is configured — every component compares exactly.
parallelRun.noComparisons: No comparison has been run yet.
parallelRun.noRegisters: No prior register has been imported yet. Start with Import a register.
parallelRun.periodMismatch: These two sides cover different pay dates. Comparing them will report differences that are really a period mismatch.
parallelRun.emptyRegister: This register holds no employees. A comparison against it will report "Nothing was compared", not a clean result.
parallelRun.unmappedWarning: Columns in this register were never mapped:
parallelRun.cleanNote: Every compared amount agreed to the penny, with no tolerance and no unmapped column.
parallelRun.noFindings: This comparison has no findings at all.
parallelRun.noExceptions: No exceptions — every cell matched exactly.

help.register: A register imported from the payroll system you are leaving — one pay period, one row per employee. Load it through Import & Export, resource "Prior payroll register", where you map the old system's column names onto this payroll's components.
help.payRun: The run to check against. Calculated runs count: the point of a parallel run is to prove the numbers before the money leaves. A draft run has no stubs and cannot be compared.
help.compared: Employees present on BOTH sides, out of each side's own count. A comparison that compared nobody is reported as "Nothing was compared", never as agreement.
help.unmapped: Columns in your file that no component claimed. Nothing in them is compared, so an amount could be sitting there unaccounted for. Re-import with them mapped, or confirm they carry no money.
help.tolerance: Every component compares exactly unless somebody configured an allowance for it. Any allowance in force is shown here and on the comparison, because a tolerance nobody can see would defeat the whole exercise.
help.unattributed: The part of the net difference the compared components do not account for. Anything other than zero means an amount moved a total with no comparable component behind it — most often a source column nobody mapped.
help.toleranceSlot: The component, or one of the register's stated totals. A tolerance is per employee, per period.
help.toleranceAmount: An absolute amount, never a percentage: a percentage of a moving base is how a tolerance quietly grows. Zero removes the allowance.
help.toleranceReason: Required. Agreeing to stop looking at a difference is a decision that has to be attributable to somebody and a reason.

workSchedules.title: Work schedules
workSchedules.description: The hours and days each employee is normally scheduled to work. Several jurisdictions compute statutory holiday pay from this — a normal working day's wages — and will refuse to calculate rather than assume an eight-hour day for someone whose schedule is not recorded.
workSchedules.drawerDescription: Applies from the start date until it is superseded or ended. Holiday pay for a past period always resolves against the pattern in force then, never today's.

pattern.cycleHint: A cycle of days that repeats — seven days for an ordinary week, fourteen for a compressed fortnight, eight for a four-on four-off rotation.
pattern.variesHint: No regular schedule; hours are set period by period. This is a real answer, not a blank one — several jurisdictions pay a varying-hours employee by a different formula, and recording it is what lets them calculate.

summary.total: {hours} hours over {days} working days per cycle.

help.scope: The most specific schedule wins: one employee beats a job title, which beats a trade, then a department, then a subsidiary, then everyone. The same order wages and entitlement limits resolve in.
help.effectiveFrom: Compared against the WORK DATE, never today. Someone who moves from full time to part time in March still has January's holiday pay computed on the full-time pattern.
help.pattern: Whether the employee works a repeating pattern, or has no regular schedule at all. The difference decides which formula several jurisdictions use.
help.cycleDays: How many days before the pattern repeats. Seven is the ordinary week. Fourteen expresses a nine-day fortnight; eight expresses a four-on four-off rotation that deliberately never lines up with the week.
help.cycleAnchor: The day the cycle starts counting from. For a weekly pattern this is a Sunday, so the boxes below are labelled Sunday to Saturday.
help.hours: The hours normally worked at each position of the cycle. Leave a day blank for a day off. These hours are what a normal working day's holiday pay is calculated from, so a four-day ten-hour week is worth ten hours a holiday, not eight.
